raw_response:
I'm 63 this year, been farming since I was 18 — that's 45 years on this land. My husband and I have just 3 mu in Quzhou, not much, but it's what we have. Our son works at a factory in Handan, so it's mostly the two of us now. We're getting old, but 3 mu we can still manage ourselves. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those agricultural books. I watch, I remember, and I talk to my neighbors.

**Winter wheat** — I always plant around October 10th, same as everyone in the village. If you plant too early the wheat grows too tall before winter and freezes; too late and it doesn't establish well. I use about one bag of wheat seed for the 3 mu — roughly 12 or 13 jin per mu. I saved most of my seed from last year's harvest, but I bought half a bag of new seed to mix in because the saved seed was looking a bit dark. Fertilizer is expensive now, so I have to be careful. I bought one bag of compound fertilizer — the kind with the three numbers on it — and spread it before planting. That's about 15 or 16 jin per mu. Then in the spring, when the wheat is at jointing and looks a bit yellow, I topdress with one bag of urea, again about 15 or 16 jin per mu. I know some people put more, but my neighbor Lao Zhang put two bags of urea on his wheat last year and it all lodged over in the wind. Waste of money. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once in March or April at jointing, and once when the grain is filling in May. Each time the pump runs it costs me — the tube well water isn't free — but you can't skip it. For weeds, if I see too many in spring I spray a herbicide once. Last year I didn't need to, but I'll watch.

**Summer maize** — As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we cut it, till quickly with our small tiller, and plant the maize. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 3 jin per mu, because saved maize seed doesn't grow right. I put down one bag of urea at planting time — about 15 or 16 jin per mu — and then I hope for rain. If July is dry and the corn is tasseling, I'll irrigate once, maybe twice if it gets really bad. The pumping cost adds up, so I watch the sky first. For pests, I don't spray unless I see armyworms or borers. Chemicals cost money, and at my age I don't like breathing that stuff unless I have to.

We do all the work ourselves — planting, carrying fertilizer bags, irrigating, harvesting. I don't hire labor for 3 mu; what would people think? My husband helps with the heavy lifting, but I manage the decisions. I know every corner of these 3 mu.

If the weather is normal, I expect about 400 jin of wheat per mu and maybe 450 to 500 jin of maize per mu. Not the highest in the village, but enough to feed us and sell a little. I don't take big risks. Change is dangerous. I do what worked last year unless I see a very good reason not to.
